May we hear with our ears what is auspicious, O Gods; may we see with our eyes what is auspicious, O Holy Ones. With firm limbs and bodies, praising you, may we attain that lifespan ordained by the Gods.

May Indra, of far-reaching fame, grant us well-being; may Pūṣan, the knower of all, grant us well-being; may Tārkṣya, whose wheel-rims are unharmed, grant us well-being; may Bṛhaspati bestow well-being upon us. *Oṃ*. Peace! Peace! Peace!

[1-1-1] Oṃ! May we hear with our ears what is auspicious, O Gods; may we see with our eyes what is auspicious, O Holy Ones. With firm limbs and bodies, praising [you], may we attain that lifespan ordained by the Gods.

May Indra of far-reaching fame grant us well-being; may Pūṣan, the all-knowing, grant us well-being; may Tārkṣya, whose wheel-rims are uninjured, grant us well-being; may Bṛhaspati bestow well-being upon us. From every water, from every source—here and there—from every [source of danger], [protect us]. 1.

Agni, Vāyu, and Sūrya have together performed this rite with inspired wisdom (*ṛtviyā*). They whose horses are the winds, who are lords of the rays, whose self is the light-rays (*marīci*), and who are free from malice—O divine ones, progenitors of the world, grant me the state of having sons.

The Mahānāmnīs, of great measure; from greatness, [they are] the light of heaven. O goddesses, born of Parjanya, grant me offspring for the sake of having sons. || 2 ||

[1-1-3] May they drive away heat, may they drive away the Rakṣas; may they drive away fever, may they drive away sin. May they drive away consumption and misfortune; may they drive away the god-sent plague.

May the divine ones drive away the thunderbolt and the Aṃśus. May the divine mothers of the world [drive away] the world. [May they drive away] the Ādityas and the goddess Aditi. From the womb, may they look upward. May the divine waters and the plants be auspicious and most peaceful. May Sarasvatī be well-disposed.
May it not appear to you in the sky. || 3 || From that [source], two [types of] medicinal herbs for the son. || 1 ||

[1-2-1] Tradition (smṛti), perception (pratyakṣa), oral tradition (aitihya), and inference (anumāna)—this fourfold means of knowledge establishes the solar orb. The sun draws forth its rays from above the entire world; by the specific nature of their ripening, time is defined as a particularization. Just as a certain river flows inexhaustibly from its source, so does [time flow]. 4.

The rivers flow toward them; the *ūrj* (vigorous power) does not turn back. Even so, those things arising from various sources—whether minute or great—are all dependent upon the year (*saṃvatsara*). All are bound together by these [elements] and pervaded by them all; the *ūrj* does not turn back. One should know that which is beyond the year; that indeed is the defining characteristic. 5.
[1-2-3] By means of both the small and the great, the year is perceived through direct observation as having ascended [to its full extent].

A supreme being (adhisattva) is not seen; it is a cloth that is discolored and brownish-yellow—this is the mark of Varuṇa. Wherever this is observed, one is led to a thousand [worlds]. Having a single head but various faces—that is the complete mark of the Seasons (Ṛtu).

[1-2-4] There are seven organs on both sides. Indeed, what is spoken is spread abroad. The white and the black belong to the year, on its right and left sides. Of this, there is this verse: "One of your forms is bright, the other is holy; you are like the sky with two days of different colors."
"For you protect all magical powers, O self-dependent one; may your bounty here be auspicious, O Pūṣan. In this [verse], there is no world, nor Pūṣan, nor cattle.
One should not perceive the year itself as the most beloved form of the Sun. Indeed, this is the most beloved form of the year:
when some great misfortune is about to befall him, [the Sun says], "Perform this meritorious act."
One should give him that as a reward. || 7 ||
As well as the characteristics, the characteristics of the seasons, and the seven worlds. || 2 ||

[1-3-1] They say that among those born together, the seventh is born alone; that the six are the seers born of the gods. Their desired abodes have been established according to their places; they tremble in their various forms before the Sustainer. Who indeed, O mortals, is not deceived?

A friend spoke to a friend: "Who is it that seeks to harm us? He who has abandoned a friend who knows him as a friend—of him there is no share even in what is spoken. Even if he hears, he hears in vain. (8)
[1-3-2] "For he has not found the path of the well-done," so it is said. Impelled by one season after another, he roars as he rushes forward.
There are sixty and thirty bridles; both the white and the black are sixty-day-old [grains]. Jaradākṣa is clad in garments of fine cloth.
Spring together with the Vasus;
[he is] the first one remembered as the utterer of the *praiṣa* (summons) for the year-long Savitṛ sacrifice. "Impel those others," [says] another. 9.
And these two protect them;
these very words are employed wherever this is observed. One should understand it to be exactly this.

This is the measure regarding the succession of time; we shall, however, explain the specific details—learn those concerning the seasons. The host of Rudras, clad in white garments, returns together with the summer, subduing the entire earth.

[1-3-4] By means of his incomparable light, he [wears] garments of every form. Learn of the Ādityas: they are the fruit of the ritual performed over a year, bestowed together with the rains. Though free from suffering, he appears as if possessed by suffering; though not yellowed, he appears as if yellowed. Without being pained by cold, he appears as if weeping. His eyes gladden both when he blazes and when he is extinguished.
Indeed, those creatures who fall away fall away after a year.
Those which find their foundation do so in the year; that is to say, in the rains. He hears all others, and six as well. 3. 11.

[1-4-1] It is precisely for one whose suffering has arisen from the eyes that [this is prescribed]. When the pupils are clear, there is no ointment for the eyes. Listen to that of the Ṛbhus: "Listen to the garments that have the luster of gold; listen to the unwashed [robes]. Eat food; cleanse yourselves. I am the giver of life to you. These words are employed when autumn is observed there. 12.
[1-4-2] Taittirīya-Āraṇyaka - Searchable Text, Page 4 of 155 - 25.11.2005 - www.sanskritweb.net/yajurveda Shaking [the dust] as if striking [it], the hosts of Maruts are possessed of wind.

From that distance, he was seen like the point of an arrow; he appeared fully armored along with them. With their skin colors faded as if by disease, they were matted-haired ascetics wearing quivers. One should know that the eyes of one who is about to fight, though not yet angry, become red like those of one who is enraged; they are like the two eyes of a bird of prey. 13.
Famine shall prevail in the worlds of the gods; water shall remain in the houses of men. Uttering these words, the lightning-flashes of the winter season depart.
Agni Pavamāna beheld them, seeing no means of livelihood here. For him, this [verse] occurs:
"Hither, hither, O Maruts, you of fervent penance, sun-skinned, I choose your far-extending shelter. (14) "As it were, I behold it; I choose it. (4)
The garments are deep red; the *aṣṭivajrī* and the *śataghnī*—
the All-Gods (*viśve devāḥ*) carry them away, they who have Agni for their tongue and are unfailing.

Neither god nor mortal, neither the all-pervading King Varuṇa, nor Agni, nor Indra, nor Pavamāna—nothing at all exists as its mother. One end of the divine bow rests in heaven; the other is fixed upon the earth. 15.

Indra himself, in the form of an ant, cut the bowstring of that [bow]. That is the Indradhanus (Indra’s bow), which is called "the unstrung" (*ajya*) among those things with the color of clouds. This very same [bow] belongs to Śaṃyu Bārhaspatya; this is the bow of Rudra.
It was indeed the tip of Rudra’s bow that crushed his head;
it became the Pravargya. Therefore, he who sacrifices with the sacrifice accompanied by the Pravargya restores the head of Rudra.
He does not become subject to disease or affliction by Rudra, he who knows thus. 16.
Resorting [to them], one sacrifices; and there are three. || 5 ||
With his eyes turned far upward and looking sideways, Śiśira appears;
neither his form nor his garments can be discerned.

The eye is not seen; indeed, they are not washed by one another. That is the characteristic of the gods. Red in the eyes, with variegated heads, toward the rising of the sun—you make a gesture of salutation; you act according to your own desire. 17.
[[1-6-2]] "Let these attend upon my speech," said Nijānukāmāñjali.
To him all the seasons bow down; he attains the office of domestic priest because he establishes the boundaries. The Brāhmaṇa who knows thus attains it.
Indeed, throughout this year, together with these commanders, he carries all the desires to Indra;
he is the drop (drapsa). Of him, there is this [verse]: || 18 ||

[1-6-3] A dropless [horse] stood upon the *aṃśumatī* river; the black one, moving along with ten thousand [followers]. Indra, by his power, [overcame] him who was blowing [the wind] toward the whirlpool. "Slay him, O thou of manly mind, the destroyer!"—with this very [hymn], Indra, together with the *salāvṛkī*, struck down the Asuras.
The *aṃśumatī* is the earth.
The year and heaven are established upon that [truth]. Teachers and students who know this must not harbor malice toward one another; whoever harbors malice falls from the heavenly world.
Thus end the circles of the seasons; the solar circles are narrative tales; from here onwards, they are accompanied by etymological explanations. 19.
It becomes *ni-jānuka* for those who act with malice, and [it consists of] five [syllables]. || 6 ||
[1-7-1] Āroga, Bhrāja, Paṭara, Pataṅga.
*Taittirīya-Āraṇyaka* – Searchable Text, Page 6 of 155 – 25.11.2005 – www.sanskritweb.net/yajurveda
"Svarṇara, Jyotiṣmat, Vibhāsa—
all these shine toward the sky for him, milking out nourishment without faltering. Kaśyapa is the eighth.
He does not leave Mahāmeru.
This thought occurs to him:
"O Kaśyapa, that art of yours which is radiant, powerful, abundant, and brilliant, in which the seven suns are placed together. (20)
[1-7-2] "Upon this [altar], let us settle the King," they say.
All these [priests] obtain light from Kaśyapa for him. Soma expels them from Kaśyapa, just as one who has failed in his work [is expelled]. Thus it is.
The vital breaths (*prāṇa*) are the living beings, the living beings who possess the senses. There are seven vital breaths located in the head.
"They are the suns," say the teachers. "I have seen these seven suns," said Pañcakarṇa Vātsyāyana and Saptakarṇa Plākṣi. || 21 ||
"O Kaśyapa, only that which is heard through tradition (ānuśravika) is for us. Thus both are made known.
Indeed, they were as if unable to go to Mahāmeru. I saw this solar disc revolving; Gārgya was saved by his vital breath (*prāṇa*).
As they were going to Mahāmeru, they left one behind.

The radiant cloth, the sun, and the firefly remain stationary yet give off heat; therefore, in this world, those who have been heated by the fires of austerity are called "heated" (taptatapāḥ). || 22 ||
[1-7-4] "In the other world," and so on; therefore, here [in this world], they are heated by the heat.
Regarding them, there is this verse:

"Seven suns have entered the sky; the giver of sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇāvān) follows them along their paths. They all heat clarified butter for him, yielding nourishment without failing. Regarding this, the teachers say that the seven officiating priests (ṛtvij) are the suns. Of these, there is this verse:
"The seven directions have various suns. (23)
[1-7-5] There are seven priests, the *hotṛ*s.
*Taittirīya-Āraṇyaka* – Searchable Text, Page 7 of 155 – 25.11.2005 – www.sanskritweb.net/yajurveda
"The seven Āditya gods— by them, O Soma, protect [me].
This also is the traditional scripture (āmnāya).
Digbhrāja creates the seasons;
by this very procedure, [he attains] the state of a thousand suns—so says Vaiśaṃpāyana. Of this, there is this verse:
"O Indra, if there were a hundred heavens and a hundred earths for you..."
Or even if there were thousands of suns, O Wielder of the Thunderbolt. || 24 ||
[1-7-6] "The two worlds have not been born after [him]," it is said.
Because the seasons possess different characteristics (*liṅga*), there is a plurality of suns.
"But the eight are determined.
There are eight solar disks above that;
of these, this is the verse:
The brilliant array of the gods has risen,
the eye of Mitra, Varuṇa, and Agni;
it has filled the heaven, the earth, and the intermediate space.
"The Sun is the soul of the moving and the stationary. || 25 ||
Together with Plākṣi, Taptritapa, Nānāsūrya, and nine Sūryas. || 7 ||

Where does this cloud enter? Where is this year intermingled with it? Where is the day, O God, and where is this night? Where are the months and the seasons situated? Where are the half-months and the moments, along with the twinklings of an eye and the infinitesimal divisions of time? Where do these waters settle when they flow forth from here at this very moment?
The dark ones dissolve into the waters; the waters are contained within the sun. 26.

The clouds resort to the waters; the lightning is contained within the sun. These two colorless worlds—this earth and yonder sky—are the two *rodasī*. What being is there between them by which these two are held apart? By Viṣṇu are the two worlds held apart.
Such was the feeling of Vatsa:
"For she has become rich in water and rich in cattle; providing excellent pasture for man, she is worthy of praise. (27)

[[1-8-3]] *Taittirīya-Āraṇyaka* - Searchable Text, Page 8 of 155 - 25.11.2005 - www.sanskritweb.net/yajurveda Viṣṇu propped apart these two worlds; he has firmly established the earth on all sides with his rays. What do they say is that strength of Viṣṇu?

What is the radiance? What is the supreme goal? That which the one God sustained—both heaven and earth tremble before it. They say that strength comes from Vāyu, and radiance is said to come from the Imperishable (Akṣara). The God sustained that which consists of three quarters: that which is the single, highest [quarter] of Viṣṇu. || 28 ||

The fires and the winds—this is his ultimate resort. I ask you about supreme death, the lowest, and the middle, as well as the world of merits and sins; this I ask you now. They call that [wind] supreme death, Pavamāna is the middle, Agni alone is the lowest death, and the moon is said to be the fourth.

[1-8-5] Those who are without focused effort go to supreme death; the wicked always go [there]. But those with focused effort go indeed to that place where the people who have performed meritorious deeds reside.
Then they come toward the middle, and they encounter the four fires. I ask you about the evildoers, where Yama makes them suffer;
O Brahman, tell us that, if you know the abodes of the wicked.

The suns risen from Kaśyapa always destroy evil in the regions between heaven and earth. There they are stationed by the Vasus; they proceed bodiless, according to their meritorious deeds—without hands, feet, or hair; there those people are born without a womb.
Having died, they undergo death once again, being devoured by their own karmas. (31)
[[1-8-7]] *Taittirīya-Āraṇyaka* - Searchable Text, Page 9 of 155 - 25.11.2005 - www.sanskritweb.net/yajurveda:
Like the *āśātikā* worms.
Then they are purified by the Vasus.
He who knows thus departs from death and conquers it.
Such indeed is that Brāhmaṇa. He is preeminent in long learning; he is a guest of Kaśyapa, one who has attained the power of going at will and the power of coming at will. Of him this [verse] occurs:
"In whom the seven Vasus..."
The ancient plants sprout forth. || 32 ||

[1-8-8] "The seer is indeed the most far-famed; Indra’s Gharma is his guest. Kaśyapa is the beholder, because he beholds everything due to his subtlety. Now, concerning the fire consisting of eight persons:
Of him, there is this [verse]: "O Agni, lead us by a good path to wealth,
O God, you who know all ways."
"Drive away from us the crooked sin; we shall offer you the most abundant utterance of homage. (33)
Concentrated, she is praised as the highest; she is called "the ancient one who has grown within the houses" by means of her own deeds. || 8 ||
Agni and Jātavedas,
the one born of strength, the swift, the lord.
Vaiśvānara and Naryāpās; Paṅktirādhas is the seventh; Visarpi is the eighth among the fires.

These eight are the Vasus who dwell upon the earth. Just as the flames of fire have specific colors according to the season—such as blue flame and yellow flame—so too are the eleven wives of Vāyu, who has eleven husbands, resplendent and pure white.
[1-9-2] And those which belong to Vāsuki and the lightning—those that are silver-colored, rough, dark, tawny, and deep red;
those that move upward and those that fall downward. There are eleven such lightning-serpents. The lightning does not strike him who knows this.
Vyāsa, the son of Parāśara, said: "I chose death by lightning; for it does not strike one who is free from desire."
He who knows thus. *Taittirīya-Āraṇyaka* – Searchable Text, Page 10 of 155 – 25.11.2005 – www.sanskritweb.net/yajurveda [[1-9-3]]

Now, the hosts of Gandharvas: Svāñcabhrāt, Aṅghāri, Bambhāri, Hasta, Suhasta, Kṛśānu, Viśvāvasu, Mūrdhanvat, and Sūryavarcas; and Kṛti—these are the eleven hosts of Gandharvas. And the Devas, the Mahādevas, the Raśmis, and the Garagiras Devas. (36)
Poison does not harm him who knows this.

"Gaurī has lowed, fashioning the waters; she is one-footed, two-footed, four-footed, eight-footed, nine-footed, having become thousand-syllabled in the highest heaven. This is a qualification of Speech (vāc). Now, those which are explained by their very utterance (nigada) shall be enumerated in order: "The boars of their own austerity... (37).
The Vidyunmahas, the Dhūpaya,
the Śvāpaya, and the Gṛhamedha— these are they.

"And these seven Parjanyas, who are the haters of the Ashmaka-vidveshas, rain upon the earth with rains. By this very [verse], they are shown to have reversed case-endings; impelled by the seven winds, they rain upon those worlds. Of them, there is this verse: "This water is the same... (38).

With high and low voices, the rain-clouds quicken the earth; the fires quicken the heavens. That syllable created by the beings, which all the gods worship—the Great Seer, they made Jamadagni its protector. Jamadagni is nourished by the meters that increase by four syllables each, being satiated by King Soma. 39.
Taittirīya-Āraṇyaka - Searchable Text, Page 11 of 155 - 25.11.2005 - www.sanskritweb.net/yajurveda [[1-9-7]] By means of the powerful Brahman.
May the quarters and the intermediate directions be auspicious for us. We choose that peace and well-being for the sacrifice.
May there be a path for the lord of the sacrifice;
may there be divine well-being for us;
may there be well-being from human beings.
May the healing medicine ascend upward;
may it be well with our bipeds, and well with our quadrupeds.
"O Soma-drinkers! O non-Soma-drinkers!"—these are explained by the *nigada* itself. || 40 ||
The pure waters of those who have practiced austerities destroy the poison of the mountains; when they are satisfied, the four-footed creatures and one [the snake] are likewise [satisfied].
This earth has a thousandfold covering;
the highest heaven has a thousandfold covering.
The Aśvins, the Nāsatyas,
are the lords of the entire moving world;
Earth is the wife, and the Sky is the husband.
Coupling, you two have overcome [the obstacles];
the son is Bṛhaspati, Rudra;
Saramā is the female and male.
One has vomited up the bright, the other has vomited up the sacrificial offering; you two are like heaven, being of different forms during the day and night. 41.

"You indeed existed first; you, being first, perform this. Having taken [the earth] from here, he [took] the waters. || 93 ||
With joined palms, he placed [the brick] in front, saying: "Even so, indeed, even so."
Then the sun rose;
that was the eastern direction. Then Aruṇaketu placed [the fire] from the south, saying: "Even so, O Agni."
Then Agni rose up from that;
she became the southern direction. Then Aruṇaketu placed [the brick] in the west with the words, "Thus indeed, O Vāyu! (94).
Then the wind arose;
that was the western direction.
Then Aruṇaketu placed [the brick] from the north with the words, "Even so, O Indra.
From that, indeed, Indra arose;
that is the northern direction.
Then Aruṇaketu placed [the brick] in the middle with the words, "Thus indeed, O Pūṣan.
Thereupon Pūṣan arose; this is that very quarter.
Then Aruṇaketu placed [the brick] above with the words, "Thus indeed, O gods.
Thereupon the gods, humans, ancestors, Gandharvas, and Apsarases arose; that is the upward direction.
The drops that flew away—from them the Asuras, Rakṣases, and Piśācas arose. Therefore they were defeated;
for they originated from the scattered drops. Regarding this, this verse was spoken: || 96 ||
When the great waters came toward the embryo,
they held Dakṣa within them and brought forth the Self-existent One.
From that, these creations were emitted.
Indeed, this [world] arose from the waters;
therefore, all this is the self-existent Brahman. Therefore, all this became as if loose and as if unstable. Prajāpati, indeed, was that.
Having fashioned the self by means of the self, it entered into that very thing. Regarding this, the following verse has been recited: || 97 ||

Having fashioned the worlds, having fashioned all beings, having fashioned all the intermediate directions and the cardinal directions, Prajāpati, the first-born of Cosmic Order (*ṛta*), entered into himself by means of his own self. Having pervaded all this, having secured all, he enters into that very same [self].
Whoever knows thus. || 98 ||
"Āsīt," "atiṣṭhan," "abhūt," "apaḥ," and "vāyo"—this is the direction that has been recited; it has been recited eight times. || 23 ||
He takes four kinds of water;
for there are indeed four forms of water.
The cloud is lightning;
the thunder is rain.
He thereby secures those very things.
He takes the waters that rain during sunshine;
he places them in front.
These indeed are the waters that bestow spiritual luster (*brahmavarcasa*).
Verily, he secures spiritual luster (*brahmavarcasa*) from the very mouth; therefore, one is more endowed with spiritual luster from the mouth. || 99 ||
He takes the *kūpyā* bricks;
he places them to the south.
These waters are indeed radiant;
he thus bestows radiance upon his right side. Therefore, the right half is more radiant. He takes still waters; he places them behind.
Still waters are indeed firmly established; he thus becomes established from behind. He takes flowing waters. 100.
He places them on the north side.
Indeed, these [bricks] carry power, as it were; they are as if rising up, as if crying out, as if running. Verily, he bestows power upon his north side.
Therefore, the latter half is more vigorous. He takes the *saṃbhāryā* bricks; he places them in the middle.
This indeed is the gathering;
he finds firm support in this very [earth].
He takes [the water] from a pool.
He places them on top. || 101 ||

He establishes himself in this very [place]. He places them in the quarters;

Or food is water;
for from water food is born— namely, that which is born from water as food.
I obtain that.
Indeed, the seers known as the Aruṇas, the Ketavas, and the Vātaraśanas built this very altar; therefore, it is called the Āruṇaketuka.
Regarding this, the following verse has been recited:
"The ruddy banners... [[1-24-5]]
"The seers with girdles of wind;
a hundredfold foundation indeed; composed, [we reach] the one who provides a thousandfold sustenance. He who piles this fire-altar finds a firm foundation by the hundreds and by the thousands.
Whoever knows this thus. || 103 ||
He takes the bricks called *brahmavarcasitaras* and places them on top; these, together with the *āruṇaketuka*, amount to eight.
Having dug out the northern altar (uttaravedi) knee-deep,
he fills it with water.
For the sake of completeness, he places the lotus leaf, the gold disk, and the person. The lotus leaf is indeed austerity;
the gold disk is truth; the person is immortality. Truly, there is only this much: as much as this exists, so much indeed is all that exists. || 104 ||
He wins that. He places a tortoise;

verily he wins the essence of the waters. And also for the attainment of the world of heaven. "All the waters, from this one, from that one, from here, from there—Agni, Vāyu, and Sūrya have fashioned them with power through wisdom. The horses are Vāyu's, they are the lords of the rays.
Fill the world; fill the gap. || 105 ||
[[1-25-3]] Those which are the three supreme births.
"Indraghoṣā vaḥ with the Vasus, come hither!"—with these words he lays down five layers. The fire-altar consists of five parts;
as great as the fire-altar is, so much of it he thus builds.
He lays down the second brick with the *lokaṃpṛṇā* verse. The Virāj consists of five feet;
of that [Virāj], this [earth] is one foot, and the intermediate space is one foot.
Heaven is one foot;
the quarters are one foot;
that which is beyond the dust of the atmosphere is one foot.
He who piles this fire-altar, and he who knows it thus, stands firm as if in sovereignty. || 106 ||
There is the *pṛṇā* [hymn]; the intermediate space (*antarikṣa*) is one foot; and there are six [verses]. || 25 ||
Having led forward the fire and kindled it,
he places these bricks around it.
In the Agnihotra, in the Darśapūrṇamāsa sacrifices,
in the Paśubandha, and in the Cāturmāsya sacrifices;
moreover, they say:

"In all sacrificial rites," [it is said]. Now Āruṇi Svāyambhuva said: "The entire fire belongs to Sāvitra"; we consider this to be without further connection, for their powers are indeed distinct. Which fire does one pile? || 107 ||

[1-26-2] One who piles the *satriya* fire—what fire does he pile? One who piles the *sāvitra* fire—what fire does he pile? One who piles the *nāciketa* fire—what fire does he pile? One who piles the *cāturhotriya* fire—what fire does he pile? One who piles the *vaiśvasṛja* fire—what fire does he pile? 108.
[1-26-3] "While piling the swift Agni for the recitation of the invitatory verses, what Agni does he pile? He piles this Āruṇaketuka Agni. For Agni is indeed a bull;
he would cause the bulls to leap about.

His sacrifice would be destroyed; therefore, one should not append [the *anuyāja*s]. One should pile [the fire-altar] in those sacrifices (*kratu*) that involve an *uttaravedi*. For the fire is piled upon the *uttaravedi*. One desiring offspring should pile it. 109.

This fire-altar belongs to Prajāpati; creatures belong to Prajāpati. He who knows this becomes possessed of offspring. One who desires cattle should pile it. Water is indeed the meeting place of cattle.
He piles the fire-altar in the consciousness of cattle; he becomes possessed of cattle, he who knows thus. 110.
One who desires rain should pile [the altar].
Water, indeed, is rain.
Parjanya becomes a showerer of rain for one who knows thus.
One who is afflicted by disease should pile [the fire-altar];
water is indeed the remedy; he thus provides a remedy for him, and he attains a full span of life. One practicing sorcery should pile [it].
The waters are indeed the thunderbolt. 111.
He hurls the very thunderbolt at his rivals; he strikes them down.
One who desires brilliance, one who desires fame, one who desires spiritual luster, and one who desires heaven should pile [the fire-altar]. Indeed, this much is all that exists.
As much as this, as much as exists—that he secures for himself. This is his vow: when it rains, he shall not run.
[1-26-7] Water is indeed immortality. [This is] for the sake of not interrupting the continuity of immortality. One should not void urine or excrement in water; one should not spit;
one should not bathe naked.

This fire is indeed secret;
it is for the sake of this fire not being over-burnt.
One should not step upon lotus leaves or gold,
so that one does not ascend this fire.
One should not eat the flesh of a tortoise.
For one who piles this fire-altar, even waters that are not free from harm become harmless to him; the waters themselves become free from harm.
Whoever knows this thus. || 113 ||
"He piles it up, he piles it up," [it is said]. One who desires offspring should pile it up if he knows thus. He should run toward water and eat four [mouthfuls]. 26.

[1-27-1] May we, together with Indra and all the gods, bring these worlds to fulfillment. May Indra, along with the Ādityas, bring our sacrifice, our bodies, and our progeny to fulfillment. May Indra, accompanied by the Ādityas and the host of Maruts, be the protector of our persons. Float up! Float away! Become light! Do not sink down again and again. Turn back toward your own city, which begins with happiness and ends in sorrow. 114.
The rays of Svāyambhuva, who fashioned bodies—
may they fashion this body for you.
Let it not be revealed to you; let it not fail. Arise, do not sleep; seek Agni, O Bhāratas, being satiated with King Soma and in harmony with the Sun and the Dawns.
Young and well-attired is he;
the eight-wheeled, nine-gated [city].
[1-27-3] Ayodhyā is the foremost city of the gods. Its golden treasury is the heavenly world, enveloped in light.
To him who indeed knows that city of Brahman, enveloped in immortality— for him Brahmā and the Vedas bestow long life, fame, and progeny; [the city] which is brilliantly shining,
golden, and completely surrounded by glory.
Brahmā [created] a golden city in the past. || 116 ||

[1-27-4] Taittirīya-Āraṇyaka - Searchable Text, Page 32 of 155 - 25.11.2005 - www.sanskritweb.net/yajurveda She has entered the unconquerable [fortress]. She goes away, free from disease. She goes away, free from consumption.

In this world and in the next, the wise man follows after both gods and asuras. Whatever a young maiden utters softly, whatever a woman says, whatever a devoted wife speaks, and whatever is done that is unharmed—Agni penetrates all that, whether it be raw or cooked.
Whether they be performers of sacrifice or non-performers,
those who go to the heavenly world have no need for concern, provided they know Indra and Agni.

Like grains of sand they gather together, driven by the rays from this world and that; given by the *ṛṣis* and the *pṛśnis*, depart, go away, and creep out from here—those who are ancient and those who are new—manifested by days, waters, and nights. 118.

May Yama grant him a dwelling; may the men protect him, and the noble ones guard him—those who are born of unplowed land and those born of plowed land, those who are placed among maidens, among young girls, and among women who have lovers;

those who have drunk the seed and those who have drunk the embryo, and those who have been offered as oblations upon the coals. Both sons and grandsons, I now deliver to Yama, the King; may there be a hundred autumns for me. 119.

[1-27-7] May that Brahman which is to be gained—which belongs to the ancestors and to Yama, to Varuṇa and the Aśvins, to Agni and to the Maruts who dwell in the sky—be for me the fulfillment of my desires; for I am indeed that eternal one. Thus [is attained] the firmament, the glory of Brahman, and wealth as riches.
O divine waters, place the sons here. || 120 ||
The city with nine gates, Brahmā, the manifest, and eight autumns. || 27 ||
[1-28-1] Taittirīya Āraṇyaka – Searchable Text, Page 33 of 155 – 25.11.2005 – www.sanskritweb.net/yajurveda [O ye two],

you who have headless forms and vulture-headed forms— drive away Destruction! [Drive away] the one who obstructs from all sides, the white-bellied one, the one with mangled legs, and the speckled-bellied one.
With that speech, he [drives] them away:

"O Agni, destroy their very sight! Envy, malice, hunger, wrath, sorcery, and malice—they have established these. With a chariot adorned with *kiṃśuka* flowers, O Agni, destroy their very sight! (121). Twenty-eight verses ending with *viśīrṣṇīṃ*.
Sing forth to Parjanya,
the bounteous son of Heaven.
May he desire pasture for us.
Let this speech be for Parjanya, the self-ruling lord;
may it find a place within his heart. May the wind be a source of delight to us, bringing joy to all people. May the plants, protected by the gods, bear fine fruit.
Parjanya is he who provides the embryo for plants, for cows, for horses, and for women. (To Parjanya) ten [verses] each, beginning with *viśīrṣṇīm*. 122, 29.

[1-30-1] May power return to me; may life return, may fortune return; may spiritual knowledge (*brahman*) return to me; may wealth return to me. That seed of mine which today has spurted onto the earth, which has flowed into the plants, and which has entered the waters—that very thing I take back again for long life and for splendor. That seed of mine which is emitted, that which is born again within me—[may it return].
By that, make me immortal; by that, make me possessed of good offspring. (123) Furthermore, there are two [more]. (30)
From the waters, Tirodhā was born;
therein indeed is Vaiśravaṇa ever present. Hide away our rivals!
Those who consume the waters; Vaiśravaṇa [possesses] the illusory power of Tvaṣṭṛ; the chariot with a thousand seats, many wheels, and a thousand horses—having mounted it, come to our offering.
To whom all beings bring tribute—wealth, cattle, elephants, gold, and horses. (124)
May we abide in the favor of the one worthy of sacrifice;
they bear the splendor of sovereignty, with food as their mouth.
And on Mount Sudarśana and on Mount Kroñca; and on the great mountain Maināga,
extending as far as the seven vāṭṭāraga peaks.
"Saṃhāryaṃ nagaraṃ tava.
These are the mantras. The ritual procedure follows hereafter.
If one should offer an oblation:
"To Hiraṇyanābha, the piercer, belonging to Kubera—this is the oblation. (125)

"Salutation to the Lord of all beings. Then, having taken the *bali* offering, he should stand near it [and say]: "Kṣattra, Kṣattra is Vaiśravaṇa; we are Brāhmaṇas. Salutation be to you; do not harm me. Having entered into this [body], eat food. Then he should establish that fire in which he performs this rite: "Tirodhā bhūḥ! Tirodhā bhuvaḥ! (126)
May you conceal yourselves; may you conceal yourselves in Bhūr, Bhuvas, and Svar.
"May he sit in the sovereignty over all the worlds. Then one should kindle that fire upon which one performs this rite.
Tirodhā bhūḥ svāhā! Tirodhā bhuvaḥ svāhā!
Tirodhā svaḥ svāhā!
*Tirodhā bhūr-bhuvaḥ-svaḥ svāhā*.
At this time, all the oblations should be offered. || 127 ||

Even those who have mastered the Veda through the instruction of a Brāhmaṇa should employ [the study] at that time of day; even if others are asleep, one should not teach while being negligent. In this way, all goals are accomplished.

He who knows thus: "For those who do not know this, while they hunger, all their goals are not accomplished. He who is your obstructive brother has taken refuge within my heart. (Taittirīya Āraṇyaka 2.19)
Therefore, I offer this foremost portion; may it not deprive me of my goals. To me, svāhā!

We pay homage to Vaiśravaṇa, the king of kings, who overcomes by force. May he, Vaiśravaṇa, the lord of desires, grant my desires to me, who desires them. Homage to Kubera, to Vaiśravaṇa, the great king.

The dawns and the ruddy rays, the seers girt by the wind, are our foundation, for they are established in a hundred ways. May those who are concentrated in a thousandfold nourishment be auspicious and most peaceful to us—the celestial waters and the plants; O Sarasvatī, be gracious!
May the sky not appear before your eyes. || 129 ||
Bali shall have seven horses from the earth as his mounts. || 31 ||
One should observe this vow for a year,
or for two months.
In brief, this is the rule;
within that, there are specific variations of the rule:
he should touch water at the three times of day, and his food and drink should be taken only at the fourth meal-time.
Or, he may eat almsfood day after day;

he should tend the sacred fire with fuel-sticks of *udumbara* wood, reciting this Anuvāka beginning with "May my power return to me"; and he should perform his duties with water that has been drawn up and purified. 130.
[1-32-2] One who does not accumulate [possessions]:
for Agni, for Vāyu, for Sūrya.
To Brahmā, to Prajāpati;
to the Moon, to the Nakṣatras; to the Seasons, to the Year; to Varuṇa, to Aruṇa—thus are the Vrata-homas performed. The instruction is the same as for the Pravargya rite.
The seers are the Aruṇas and the Kaṇvas.
They should study in the forest, having recited the two verses beginning with "bhadraṃ karṇebhiḥ. || 131 ||
Having touched water with the Mahānāmnī verses, the teacher should give it to him.
With the verse, "May the auspicious one come to us with peace," he touches the plants; with "O kindly one," the earth.
This is likewise at the conclusion.
A cow is the sacrificial fee.
A garment of silk or linen,
or another white cloth,
according to one's means.
In this very way, according to the rule for private Vedic recitation (*svādhyāya-dharma*), one should study in the forest.

An ascetic becomes meritorious; an ascetic becomes meritorious. (132) Having performed [the ritual], and having muttered [the prayers] according to the rule for private Vedic recitation, he should do so twice. (32)

O auspicious one, let the memory of Sākaṃjā be present; [the ladles] are copper-colored, with eyes turned very high, and free from disease. Where is this fire? Spread out the filter that has a thousand turns. [The offering] belongs to the eight sources: that which belongs to Aditi, to the disease-free one, to Vāyu, and to Agni. In the south-eastern direction, Indra’s roar is yours. Of the waters, [he is] the one who is of the waters; the waters are indeed fourfold. [The water] reaching up to the knees: having led forth the fire, [one offers] to these two-headed ones for Parjanya. Again, to the waters, for a year—thirty-two [verses]. 32.

"May there be well-being through the light. In that [rite], King Aṅgiras poured down the thousandfold, the hundredfold, and the eightfold [oblations] for those falling away; he becomes the possessor of a dwelling place for them. These are the relatives of the existent. For one desiring rain, [he should offer] from the north, [using] a headless [sacrificial cake]; [there are] thirty-two [verses] and one hundred and twenty-eight [oblations]. 132.
Blessed is the ascetic; he becomes meritorious; blessed is the ascetic; he becomes meritorious.

May we hear with our ears what is auspicious, O Gods; may we see with our eyes what is auspicious, O Holy Ones. With firm limbs and bodies, praising you, may we attain that lifespan ordained by the Gods.

May Indra of far-reaching fame grant us well-being; may Pūṣan, the knower of all, grant us well-being; may Tārkṣya, whose wheel-rims are uninjured, grant us well-being; may Bṛhaspati bestow well-being upon us. *Oṃ*. Peace! Peace! Peace!
Homage to Brahman; homage be to Agni; homage to the Earth; homage to the plants; homage to Speech; homage to the Lord of Speech; homage to the great Viṣṇu—I pay it.
Oṃ. Peace, peace, peace.

[2-1-1] Indeed, the sacrifices of the gods and the Asuras were both extended simultaneously. "We shall go to the heavenly world; we shall go! they [the gods] thought. Those Asuras, having equipped themselves, proceeded with force. But the gods [proceeded] by means of celibacy (*brahmacarya*) and austerity (*tapas*). Those Asuras became deluded; they did not understand; they were defeated and did not reach the heavenly world.

[2-2-1] Indeed, the *rakṣas* stood firm against the *puronuvāka* and the *tapas*. Prajāpati invited them with a boon; they chose this boon: "The Sun shall be our warrior. Prajāpati said to them, "Fight! Therefore, these *rakṣas* indeed rise up and fight the Sun until he has set. These *rakṣas* are indeed pacified by water consecrated with the *gāyatrī*. For this reason, these exponents of the Veda (*brahmavādinaḥ*) face the east during the twilight.

They sprinkle water consecrated with the Gāyatrī; that water, having become a thunderbolt, hurls those Mandeha demons into the Aruṇa island. By walking around [the sun] clockwise, they shake off evil. A learned Brāhmaṇa who, while performing [this rite], meditates upon the sun as it rises and as it sets, attains all that is auspicious. "The sun is Brahman"—he who knows this, being Brahman itself, goes to Brahman. || 2 || || 2 ||
O gods, whatever offense against the gods we have committed,
O Ādityas, release me from that; by the truth of cosmic order, deliver me from this.
O gods, whatever untruth we have uttered through our speech out of a desire for life, from that release us here, O all-gods, acting in harmony.
By Truth, O Heaven and Earth; by Truth, O Sarasvatī.
Protect us from the sin of cooked food and whatever falsehood we have uttered.
May Indra and Agni, Mitra and Varuṇa, Soma, Dhātṛ, and Bṛhaspati—
may they release us from the sin that we have committed through others.

From the curse of a kinsman, from the curse of a relative, from the curse of one who is superior or even of one who is inferior—from that sin committed against the gods which is unassailable, O Jātavedas, release us. 3.
Whatever untruth we have committed with speech, with the mind, with the two arms, with the two thighs, with the two knees, or with the penis—
may Agni Gārhapatya release me from that sin; whatever evil deeds we have done.

By that [light] through which Trita emerged from the waters, by which he released the sun from darkness, and by which Indra cast off all enemies—with that light, attaining light, I have reached the eye. Whatever debt remains unpaid by me here, for which I wander with the treasure of Yama—by this, O Agni, I become free from debt; even while living, I restore it to you.

When my mother crushed me, when [I am in] the atmosphere, when I transgress the directions—O gods born in heaven, O Trita! When I [transgress] the waters—this prayer I offer to you, O Varuṇa; "Do thou [grant us freedom from sin]," O Agni; "Thou art such a one for us," O Agni; "Thou, O Agni, art the unswerving one. 4.
And deliver us from the seven. || 3 ||
Whatever debt I incurred while not gambling, or what I desired to withhold from people, may Agni and Indra, acting in harmony,
release me from that.

Whatever sins I have committed with my two hands, striking at the cry of the dice—may Ugrampaśyā and Rāṣṭrabhṛt, those two Apsarases, remit those debts. O Ugrampaśyā and Rāṣṭrabhṛt, whatever sins and whatever gambling losses have not been paid back, may the debt-free man, equalizing them, not be bound by the cord of Yama in his world. Loosen the lowest bond, loosen the middle one; O Varuṇa, I entreat you for this. O Agni, do thou [protect] us; O Agni, do thou [protect] us. Saṃkusuka, Vikusuka, Nirṛtha, and Niṣvana—they have driven the disease far away from us, from afar, since we are sinless.

We have driven away consumption, the sorcery, and destruction; by that we send forth against him whoever seeks to harm us. With the ill-spoken and the counter-spoken, with the strike and the follow-up strike—by these we send forth against him whoever seeks to harm us from another side.

We have united with splendor, with nourishment, and with our bodies, and with a well-disposed mind. May Tvaṣṭṛ here bestow wealth upon us and smooth over whatever in our bodies is injured. (5) [Total: 5 verses; Section 4 ends with 5 verses and 5 sections].
Bestowing life upon you from every side, may this Agni, the most excellent, grant it;
your breath returns to you; I drive away consumption for you.
O Agni, bestowing long life, enjoying the oblation, with ghee as your face and ghee as your source, come hither!

Having drunk the ghee and the sweet, pleasant product of the cow, protect this boy like a father protects his son. O Agni, make him fit for long life and splendor; O Varuṇa, sharpen his keen vigor. O Aditi, grant him protection like a mother; O All-Gods, so that he may reach old age. O Agni, you purify our lives; speed forth strength and nourishment for us. Drive far away all misfortune.
O Agni, purify yourself, O skillful one; bestow upon us splendor and heroic strength, granting me wealth and nourishment. 6.
Agni is the seer, the purifying one, the benefactor of the five peoples, the domestic priest;
we implore him for great wealth.

O Agni, Jātavedas, drive away our born enemies and repel those yet unborn; shine upon us with a gracious mind, O Unreproachable One, so that we may dwell in your triple-protected shelter. With might, drive away our born enemies and repel those yet unborn, O Jātavedas; speak for us with a benevolent heart, and may we be preeminent, driving away our foes. O Agni, the man who from all sides seeks to harm us like a wolf—slay him, O Vṛtra-slayer, and bring wealth to us.
O Agni, whoever assails us, whether he be an equal or a stranger.
Having made that our fuel, we offer it to you, O Agni. || 7 ||
He who curses us while we do not curse, and he who curses us while we are cursing—
may both Uṣas and Nirmṛk sweep away all that evil from him.

O Gods, whatever mortal enemy or adversary assails us, let not a trace of him remain, as if of a log consumed by fire. O Jātavedas, whoever hates me, and whomsoever I hate, and whoever hates me—burn them all together, O Agni, both those whom I hate and those who hate me. Whoever acts with hostility toward us, and whatever person hates us, whoever reviles us or seeks to harm us—reduce them all to ashes.
May my sacred knowledge be refined; may my vigor and strength be refined;
may my sovereign power be refined and victorious, I for whom I am the domestic priest.
I have raised up their arms, their luster, and their strength;
with my sacred word (*brahman*), I destroy the enemies and I elevate my own people.

May mind come back to me; may life-span come back to me; may sight come back to me; may hearing come back to me; may breath come back to me; may intention come back to me; may thought come back to me; may reflection come back to me.
May Vaiśvānara, the undeceivable protector of my body, drive away all misfortunes. 8.
We bestow nourishment; [there are] five and four [verses]. 5.
We announce to Vaiśvānara whatever debt or promise we have made among the gods.

May he, releasing these bonds, know us; may he release us from misfortune and reproach. May Vaiśvānara purify us with purifiers. Whatever promise I have run toward in expectation, not knowing it in my mind but entreating it—whatever sin is therein, that I cast away.

O auspicious one, these two stars in the sky named Vicṛtau—grant them this release from their bond, bestowing immortality upon them. May you loosen the worlds; make the bonds slack, for you are the releaser of the bound.

Like an embryo released from the womb, follow all paths. May he, the wise Prajāpati, the first-born of Cosmic Order (Ṛta), receive you with full knowledge. Having given yourself to us until beyond old age, may we follow the unbroken thread [of our lineage]. 9.

[2-6-2] Some follow along the extended thread, for whom what has been given as an ancestral offering provides a path. Whatever food I eat in various forms, clothing, gold, cows, goats, and sheep—
whatever debt I have toward the gods, whatever I have accepted as a gift— may Agni make me free from that debt.

[[2-7-1]] The seers known as the Vātaraśanas were ascetics who lived on air and subsisted on roots. Those seers sought them out; they wandered about in hiding and entered into the *kūśmāṇḍa* plants. By what means may we serve you in this abode? The seers said, "Tell us a purifying hymn (*pavitra*) by which we may become free from sin. They (the Vātaraśanas) beheld these hymns, beginning with *yad devā devaheḷanam*.

With the verses, "Whatever debt I have incurred while gambling," "Bestowing long life upon you from every side," and "We announce [this] to Vaiśvānara," one should offer oblations of clarified butter (*ājya*). [[2-8-1]] One who considers himself as if unpurified should offer oblations with the Kūśmāṇḍa mantras. From whatever sin short of the killing of an embryo he has committed, he is released from that. As much sin as he incurs until he enters the consecration (*dīkṣā*), he offers these oblations continuously once he is consecrated. He remains consecrated for a year; through the year itself, he purifies his self. Or he remains consecrated for a month; for a month is a year, and through the year itself, he purifies his self. He remains consecrated for twenty-four nights; there are twenty-four half-months in a year; from the year itself he purifies himself. He remains consecrated for twelve nights; there are twelve months in a year; from the year itself he purifies himself. He remains consecrated for six nights; there are six seasons in a year; from the year itself he purifies himself. He remains consecrated for three nights; the Gāyatrī has three feet; by means of the Gāyatrī itself he purifies himself. He should not eat meat.

He may approach his wife, but he should not sit upon her while she is seated above him; he should loathe untruth. Milk is the vow for a Brāhmaṇa, rice-gruel for a Rājanya, and curdled milk (āmikṣā) for a Vaiśya; furthermore, even at the Soma sacrifice, one should prescribe this as the vow. If he should think, "I shall become exhausted," he should supplement it with boiled rice, parched grains, flour-meal, and ghee, so that he does not suffer exhaustion.

[2-9-1] While the speckled goats were performing austerity, the self-existent Brahman flowed toward them; they became seers (*ṛṣi*). That is the seerhood of the seers. [2-10-1] Indeed, these five great sacrifices are continuously extended and continuously completed: the sacrifice to the gods, the sacrifice to the ancestors, the sacrifice to the spirits, the sacrifice to men, and the sacrifice to Brahman. Whatever one studies for private recitation—be it even a single Ṛc, Yajus, or Sāman—that constitutes the completion of the sacrifice to Brahman (brahmayajña). When one studies the Ṛcs, streams of milk flow for his ancestors and carry the svadhā offerings to them; when he studies the Yajuses, streams of ghee; when he studies the Sāmans, Soma flows purified for them; when he studies the Atharvāṅgirasas, streams of honey; and when he studies the Brāhmaṇas, Itihāsas, Purāṇas, Kalpas, Gāthās, and Nārāśaṃsīs, streams of fat flow and carry the svadhā offerings to his ancestors. Thus he satisfies the gods: when [he recites] the Yajus verses, he satisfies them with oblations of ghee; when the Sāmans, with oblations of Soma; when the Atharvans and Aṅgirases, with oblations of honey; and when the Brāhmaṇas, Itihāsas, Purāṇas, Kalpas, Gāthās, and Nārāśaṃsīs, he satisfies them with oblations of fat. These, being satisfied, satisfy him in turn with long life, splendor, radiance, prosperity, fame, the luster of sacred knowledge, and food. 14. 10.

One who is about to perform the *brahmayajña* (sacrifice to Brahman) should go out from the village toward the east, where the roof is no longer visible, or toward the north, or toward the northeast; when the sun has risen, having arranged the sacrificial cord over the right shoulder, having sat down, and having washed his hands, he should sip water three times, wipe his mouth twice, and touch [the organs] once—touching the head, the two eyes, the two nostrils, the two ears, and the heart. By the fact that he sips water three times, he gratifies the *ṛc*s; by the fact that he wipes his mouth twice, he gratifies the *yajus* formulas; by the fact that he touches [the organs] once, he gratifies the *sāmans*; and by the fact that he sprinkles his left hand and his feet with water, [he gratifies the Atharvans].

When he touches his head, eyes, nostrils, ears, and heart, he thereby gratifies the Aṅgirasas, the Brāhmaṇas, the Itihāsas, the Purāṇas, the Kalpas, the Gāthās, and the Nārāśaṃsīs. desire is the giver. 15.
Desire is the receiver;
O Desire, enter the ocean.
I accept you with desire; O Desire, this is yours. This, O Desire, is your sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā). May Uttaṅga Āṅgirasa accept you. [This is] a garment for Soma;
a cow for Rudra.
To Varuṇa, a horse;
to Prajāpati, a human being. || 16 ||
To Manu, a bed;
to Tvaṣṭṛ, a she-goat.
To Pūṣan, a sheep;
to Nirṛti, a mule and a donkey;
to the Himavat, an elephant; to the Gandharvas and Apsarases, a garland and ornaments; to the Viśvedevas, grain; to Vāc, food.
The rice for Brahmā; the waters for the ocean. || 17 ||
[3-10-4] For Utāna Āṅgirasa,
[he yoked] a chariot for Vaiśvānara.
Vaiśvānara has ascended to the vault of heaven, as of old,
to the back of the sky, being glorified by those of good thoughts;
he [bestows] wealth upon the living being, as in former times.
The watchful one goes around the common racecourse.
O Goddess Dakṣiṇā, may King Varuṇa lead you to Vaiśvānara on the chariot; through him, may I attain immortality. May there be vigor for the giver!
May it be for my benefit and for the one who receives it. || 18 ||
Who has given this to whom?

[3-11-1] He discovered the golden Gharma, the longing one, the self of Indra moving tenfold; he who moves within the ocean with his mind—the Brahman found him, the Daśahotṛ, in the flood. Having entered within, he is the ruler of people; being one, he spreads out in many ways.
Where the hundred pure essences become one, where all the Vedas become one, where all the Hotṛ-priests become one—he is the mental Self of people. 20.
[3-11-2] He who has entered within as the teacher of people, the Self of all— in whom all creatures become one;
where the four officiating priests reach completion with the gods— he is the mental Self of people, the Brahman, Indra, and Agni, the foundation of the world.
By day, he discovered through austerity Savitṛ, Bṛhaspati, the Caturhotṛ, and those appointed according to the quarters— the author who has entered within, the very essence of speech.
Tvaṣṭṛ, the wise one, who transforms forms.

[3-11-3] This sacrifice is the breath of immortality; the seers have discerned it as the self of the four *hotṛ*s. Having entered within, this is the agent; it is the kinship of the gods, deposited in secret places. This sacrifice is fashioned by immortality; the seers have discerned it as the self of the four *hotṛ*s. He knows all a hundred teams; possessing all boons, he encompasses this entire universe.
The five-fold Hotṛ priest is the self of Indra, established as the immortality of the gods and the life-span of living beings. 22.
[3-11-4] The wise have discerned this King Indra, Savitṛ, the very self of Vāyu; him who shines amidst the rays of light. At the station of Cosmic Order (Ṛta), the wise offer oblations.

He who, remaining unbroken, sustains the world within his atomic sheath and beholds the worlds from within; whose atomic sheath they call vigor and whose membrane is the vital breath—by that immortal one am I fashioned.
A golden sheath, enveloped by the dust [of the world], the treasure-hold of the gods, the radiant Virāj. (23)
They perceive that digit of his as full of nectar; you have not indeed failed to reach even a quarter of the sixfold oblation, by which the seasons were ordained fivefold,
or indeed sixfold, ordained by the mind.
The wise, through the seasons, establish him as the Hotṛ-priest who is being fashioned; they lead him to the station of Cosmic Order (Ṛta).
This creator has entered within; he moves by means of the mind within the moon. Though he exists together with them, the gods do not recognize him—the very self of Indra, moving in a hundred ways.
Indra is the king who rules over the world;
he is the seven-hoṭṛ, distributed sevenfold.

The thread being sprinkled by another, moving within the sun with the mind—the Brahman discovered the heart of the gods. This Brahman drew forth this [Veda] from the Brahman. The *arka* (sun) drips in the midst of the ocean, in which the seven rivers flow;
it possesses abundant glory and many horses, O Indra, and is rich in cattle. 25.
He is the infallible one who possesses abundant prosperity;
he is Hari, the best among the finders of wealth.
For me, Indra causes the cow to swell; may Indra bestow upon me abundant wealth consisting of many horses and cattle, unshakeable and manifold prosperity.
A hundred times a hundred are his harnessed bay horses; may Indra, the ray, come hither with the Vasus. Bestowing abundant glory, may Indra, the ray, Savitṛ, bestow it upon me. || 26 ||
May this Agni bestow upon me the luster of ghee, honeyed vigor, and sensory power.

Hari, the bird, the winged one, the fair-feathered, dwelling in heaven, who moves through the sky—he, our Indra, shall grant the boon we desire. The broad wheel with five spokes revolves; golden light is in the midst of the stream. The eternal light moves along, gliding through the sky—he, our Indra, shall grant the boon we desire. Seven yoke the chariot that has but a single wheel. (27)
A single horse, bearing seven names, draws [the chariot];
a wheel with three naves, undecaying and peerless, by which all these worlds stand firm. Beholding the auspicious, they drew near in the beginning.
The seers who have found the light of heaven performed austerities and consecration;

from that, the ruling power, strength, and vigor were born. May the gods favor this for him—the white ray being enjoyed, the leader of the waters, the guardian of the world—Indra, whom they perceived in the highest heaven. 28.
The ruddy ones, tawny, uniform;
flowing, tawny, uniform.
Hundreds, thousands, and millions of new [worlds]— this white ray [of light] encompasses this entire world,
as well as progeny, cattle, and wealth.
May he grant it to us.
The white ray has encompassed everything. May he produce for me cattle of every form. The bird is anointed by the magic power of the Asura. 29.

The wise behold with the heart and with the mind; within the ocean, the seers perceive. The ordainers seek the station of the rays; the bird bears speech within his mind. That [speech], the Gandharva spoke while within the womb; that shining, celestial wisdom, the seers guard at the station of Cosmic Order (*ṛta*). Whatever domestic animals there are, of every form—though diverse in appearance, they are manifold yet of one form—may the god Agni release them from Agni. (30)
Prajāpati, in harmony with his offspring—O you two, at every lock of hair, bestow [strength] upon us! Lead forth the Lord of Sacrifice further and further!

Those domestic animals which are of all forms, though diverse yet manifoldly of one form—may there be delight here for those seven, for the increase of wealth, for good progeny, and for heroic vigor! Those wild animals which are of all forms, though diverse yet manifoldly of one form... (31)

[3-11-13] May the god Vāyu release these [animals], O Agni; may Prajāpati, in harmony with his progeny, [release them]. The gods discovered the moving and unmoving world, rich in ghee, which had crept away for the sake of Iḍā and was hidden in a secret place. Those forest animals of every form—
Though diverse, they are of one form in many ways;
may there be delight here for these seven,
for the increase of wealth, for good progeny, and for great heroic power.

May the Self of men, the wise one who transforms, the sovereign of creatures, the radiant one who moves through the earth—may he bestow upon me the Gomatī, the single-wheeled heaven, and the eight forms of the One through his divine power. 11.

The Puruṣa has a thousand heads, a thousand eyes, and a thousand feet. Having pervaded the earth on every side, he transcended it by the measure of ten fingers. The Puruṣa alone is all this—whatever has been and whatever is to be; moreover, he is the Lord of immortality, which transcends what grows through food. Such is his greatness.
And greater than this is the Puruṣa. || 33 ||

One foot of him is all beings; his three feet are the immortal in heaven. With three feet the Puruṣa rose upward; one foot of him was here again. From there he strode out in all directions, toward what is eaten and what is not eaten. From him Virāj was born; from Virāj, the Puruṣa.
Once born, he surpassed [all things], both behind and before.

That [which was offered] with the Puruṣa as the oblation...
The gods performed the sacrifice;

spring was its clarified butter, summer its fuel, and autumn its oblation. Seven were its enclosing sticks, and thrice seven were the logs prepared. While the gods were performing the sacrifice, they bound Puruṣa as the victim. Upon the sacrificial grass, they sprinkled that sacrifice—Puruṣa who had been born in the beginning. 35.

By that [sacrifice], the gods, the Sādhyas, and the Ṛṣis performed worship. From that sacrifice, from which everything was offered, the speckled butter (pṛṣadājya) was gathered. He made those animals his own—both those of the forest and those of the village—from that sacrifice, from which everything was offered. From it the Ṛg-verses and the Sāman-chants were born; from it the meters (chandas) were born; from it the Yajus-formula was produced. 36.
From that, horses were born,
as well as all those animals with two rows of teeth.

From him the cows were born; from him goats and sheep were born. When they divided the Puruṣa, into how many parts did they arrange him? What was his mouth, what were his two arms, what were his thighs, and what are his feet called? The Brāhmaṇa became his mouth; the Rājanya was made his two arms. || 37 ||

[3-12-6] His thighs became the Vaiśya; from his feet the Śūdra was born. The Moon was born from his mind; from his eye the Sun was born. From his mouth Indra and Agni were born; from his breath Vāyu was born. From his navel the intermediate space arose.
From his head the sky evolved; from his feet the earth, and from his ears the quarters. In this manner they fashioned the worlds.

I know this great Person, resplendent like the sun, beyond the darkness. The Wise One, having fashioned all forms and created their names, sits calling them forth. The Creator proclaimed him in the beginning; Śakra, the wise one, [proclaimed him] in the four quarters. Knowing him thus, one becomes immortal here; there is no other path for the journey. By means of sacrifice, the gods sacrificed to the sacrifice; those were the first ordinances.
Those great ones attained the height of heaven, where the ancient Sādhyas, the gods, abide. 39.
The Puruṣa was born first, in front; having been made, he fashioned two [worlds], including the seat. || 12 ||
Greater than the person is the Person; elsewhere there is no person. He was born from the waters, from the earth, and from its essence; he arose from Viśvakarman.

Tvaṣṭṛ, fashioning his form, enters him; that is the universal birthplace of the Puruṣa in the beginning. I know this great Puruṣa, resplendent like the sun, beyond darkness. Knowing him thus, one becomes immortal here; there is no other path for the journey. Prajāpati moves within the womb; though unborn, he is born in many ways. 40.
The wise perceive his source; the sages seek the station of the rays. He who shines upon the gods, he who is the domestic priest of the gods.
Homage to him who was born before the gods; homage to the radiant one of the Brahman;
[to those] generating the radiant Brahman.
In the beginning, the gods said this:
"Whosoever among the Brahmins should know thus, the gods shall be under his control."
Modesty and Fortune are your two wives; day and night are your two sides;
the constellations are your form;
the Aśvins are your gaping mouth.
May I obtain what is desired; may I obtain that [person]; may I obtain everything. 41.
And seven more are born under one's control. || 13 ||
Being a sustainer, while being sustained himself, he sustains [others]. *Taittirīya-Āraṇyaka* - Searchable Text, Page 55 of 155 - 25.11.2005 - www.sanskritweb.net/yajurveda [[3-14-1]]
The one God has entered into many forms.

When he grows weary of bearing the burden, having laid down the burden, he goes again to his setting. Him they call Death, him they call Immortality; him they call the Sustainer, him they call the Protector.
He, being sustained and being supported, sustains all.
He who knows how to support this [breath] with truth—this one abandons him as soon as he is born;
yet it does not abandon the one who grows old. 42.
[3-14-2] Moreover,
the tireless god Prārtha brought many things into one day; he who knows that from whence he came into being.
He has joined this bond with the sacred word (*brahman*); he delights in it even when it is worn out or lying still. It does not abandon him throughout the former days.
All the waters flow toward you, knowing you, purifying themselves with milk like a calf.
You kindle Agni, the bearer of oblations;
you are Mātariśvan, the sustainer of all creatures. 43.

[3-14-3] You are the sacrifice; you indeed are Soma. All the gods come to your call. You are one who has entered into many. Homage be to you; be easy for me to invoke. Homage be to you both; hear my call. O Prāṇa and Apāna, moving together with speed, I summon you both by means of this sacred formulation (brahman) to this very moment. O youthful ones, abandon him who hates me. O Prāṇa and Apāna, being in agreement, abandon him. Do not unite with the life-breath of that man.

O gods, being in agreement with the sacred word (*brahman*), give that [weapon] to me for the sake of slaying; with that I shall strike him down. From non-being he was born, and from being he came into existence; whomever he has brought forth, he is indeed the protector of this world.

When he grew weary of bearing the burden, that burden was cast off by him and returned to its source; for you indeed became the vital breath (prāṇa). You are the great enjoyment of Prajāpati, the arm about to perform its work, since you have caused the nine gods to breathe.
One for the progeny; you two shall go forth ninefold. || 14 ||

The gods follow Hari as he carries away [the world], the bull of all thoughts, the lord of the universe. May the Brahman, which is of like form, come after me. Do not obstruct my path; stride forth! Do not cut me off, O Death; do not slay me!

Do not rob me of my strength; do not steal it from me! Do not harm my offspring; do not shorten my life! We shall worship you, the one who beholds men, with an oblation—[you] who are striving instantly.
To death that causes trembling. || 46 ||
The quarters have listened for him; through desire they have brought him forth again. Through desire has desire come to me, from heart to heart, from death. That which is their beloved there—
Therefore, let it come toward me; O Death, follow along another path, one that is distinct from the path of the gods. I speak this to you who have eyes and hear:
do not harm our progeny, nor our heroes.

Praising with my ancient mind, imploring the bull among the people, I worship Death, the first-born of Truth, who alone rules over human progeny. (47) [This section contains fifteen verses, including four concerning heroes.]
O Sūrya, you are the deliverer, visible to all, the maker of light; you illuminate the entire radiant realm.
You are taken with a support; for the radiant Sūrya, you! This is your womb; for the radiant Sūrya, you! || 48 || || 16 ||
[3-17-1] Swell, O most exhilarating Soma, with all your protections; be for us the most far-reaching. 49. 17.
Those mortals who saw the earliest Uṣas as she was shining forth have passed away; she has now become visible to us. And those who shall see her in future days—they too shall pass away. 50. 18.

I settle you, the luminous; I settle you, the maker of light; I settle you, the knower of light; I settle you, the radiant; I settle you, the blazing; I settle you, the one becoming resonant with *malmala*. *Taittirīya-Āraṇyaka* – Searchable Text, Page 57 of 155 – 25.11.2005 – www.sanskritweb.net/yajurveda

I settle you, the blazing one; I settle you, the radiant one; I settle you, the unceasing one; I settle you, the one of great light; I settle you, the awakening one; I settle you, the watchful one. || 51 || || 19 ||

To exertion, svāhā! To fatigue, svāhā! To weariness, svāhā! To exhaustion, svāhā! To rising effort, svāhā! To decline, svāhā! To the pure, svāhā! To the capable, svāhā! To the one being heated, svāhā! To the one heating, svāhā! To the murder of a Brahmin, svāhā! To everything, svāhā! 52. 20.

[3-21-1] With the mind, [he offers] to Bhava; with the liver, to Rudra; with the thin membrane, to Paśupati; with the thick heart, to Agni; with the heart, to Rudra; with the blood, to Śarva; with the two kidneys, to Mahādeva; with the inner ribs, to Aupīṣṭhahan; with the two sheaths of the intestines, [he offers]. 53. 21.

Citti; Pṛthivī; Agni; Sūrya; Cakṣus; Mahāhavis; Hotṛ; Vāk; Hotṛ; Brāhmaṇa; Ekahotṛ; Agni; Yajurbhis; Iṣṇan; Indrasya devasya; Suvarṇam; Gharma; Sahasraśīrṣā; Adbhyaḥ; Bhartā; Harim; Taraṇi; Āpyāyasva; Eyuṣṭe; Ye; Jyotiṣmatīm; Prayāsāya; Citta; Ekaviṃśatiḥ. || 21 ||
The mind is Agni; having entered within by means of the Yajus formulas, Prajāpati is in harmony with his offspring. Of him, the wise [chant] the luminous fifty-three-fold [Stoma]. 53.
The word *citti* [is used] with *śiṅgī* and *nikośya*.
We choose that which is auspicious for well-being; we choose the path for the sacrifice;
we choose the path for the lord of the sacrifice.
May there be divine well-being for us; may there be well-being from human beings. May the healing medicine ascend upward. May it be auspicious for our bipeds; may it be auspicious for our quadrupeds.
Oṃ. Peace, peace, peace.
Homage! May they rejoice after me.
Oṃ. Peace, peace, peace.

Homage to Speech, both that which is uttered and that which is unuttered; homage to that Speech! Homage to Speech! Homage to the Lord of Speech! Homage to the seers, the makers of mantras, the lords of mantras! May the seers, the makers of mantras, the lords of mantras, not abandon me; may I not abandon the seers, the makers of mantras, the lords of mantras. May I utter speech sacred to all the gods—speech that is auspicious, harmless, and pleasing to the deities. May Heaven grant me protection; may Earth grant me protection; may this entire world grant me protection. May the Moon and the Sun grant me protection; may Brahmā and Prajāpati grant me protection.

I shall speak of what has been; I shall speak of the world; I shall speak of splendor; I shall speak of fame; I shall speak of austerity; I shall speak of the Veda; I shall speak of truth. Therefore, O spreader, I spread this for you as a spreading;
let there be a spreading for me.

May I be a spreading carpet for offspring and cattle; may I become [such] for offspring and cattle. O out-breath and in-breath, protect me from death! O out-breath and in-breath, do not desert me! I shall conceive honey, I shall give birth to honey, I shall speak honey, I shall utter honey. May I raise up speech full of honey for the gods and worthy of being heard by men. May the gods protect me for the sake of splendor; may the fathers rejoice after me. Om. Peace, peace, peace. 1.

[4-2-1] They harness the mind, and they harness the thoughts—the inspired singers of the great, inspired, wise one. He alone, the knower of the ways, ordains the priestly functions. Great is the praise of the god Savitṛ. At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, I take thee up. Thou art the spade; thou art the woman. Performer of the sacrifice for the gods! Arise, O Brahmaṇaspati! 2.
[4-2-2] Seeking you, O God, we pray; may the bounteous Maruts come hither.
O Indra, be a swift sharer with us.
Let Brahmanaspati go forward;
let the divine Sūnṛtā go forward.
O gods, lead our sacrifice toward the hero, the benefactor of men, who bestows fivefold wealth. O divine Heaven and Earth, be mindful of me; may I prosper today.
This is the head of Makha. 3.
[4-2-3] For Makha thee;
for the head of Makha thee.
So great wast thou at first;
may I prosper today.
The head of Makha.
For Makha thee!
For the head of Makha thee!
O divine ants, first-born of this being, observers of the cosmic order (*ṛta*), may I prosper today through your success!
The head of Makha. || 4 ||
[4-2-4] For Makha thee! For the head of Makha thee! Thou art the vigor of Indra. May I prosper today! The head of Makha.
For Makha thee! For the head of Makha thee! Thou art born of Agni; thou art the seed of Prajāpati. May I prosper this day. The head of Makha. 5.
For Makha thee!
For the head of Makha thee!
Bestow life; bestow breath. Bestow the out-breath; bestow the diffused breath. Bestow sight; bestow hearing.
Bestow mind; bestow speech. Bestow the self; bestow a firm foundation. Bestow me; bestow me within yourself.
May honey make you sweet. You are the head of Makha. 6.
[4-2-6] You two are the feet of the sacrifice. I fashion you with the Gāyatrī metre.
I fashion you with the Triṣṭubh metre; I fashion you with the Jagatī metre;
you are the girdle of Makha.
May Aditi take hold of your opening;
with the Pāṅkta metre,
may you be heated by the heat of the sun.
You are Makha. || 7 ||

O cloth, protect my head! May I prosper today through the head of Makha. You are the head, the head, the head—nine [syllables]. So great are the goddesses; you are the vigor of Indra; you are born of Agni; bestow life-span, bestow breath—five [syllables].
[4-3-1] You are the residue of the vigorous horse. May Varuṇa, whose vows are firm, fumigate you with the steadfast law of Mitra and Varuṇa. For the flame, you! For the radiance, you!
For light thee!
For heat thee!
Surpass this heaven with thy greatness!
Mitra became far-extending, and [he overspread] the earth with his glory. 8.
Of Mitra, the supporter of the people, the glory of the god is winning; his splendor is most wonderful in renown. For success, I take you.

May Savitṛ, the god with beautiful hands, beautiful fingers, and beautiful arms, raise you up by his power, so that you may not fall upon the earth; fill the regions and the quarters; arise and become great! 9.
[4-3-3] Stand upright; you are firm. I gaze upon you with the eye of the Sun. For the straight, for the good, I take you.
For well-being thee, for prosperity thee!
Here do I enclose this one, the son of such-and-such a father, with the people, with cattle, and with the splendor of sacred knowledge (*brahmavarcasa*). I cover thee with the *gāyatrī* metre;
I cover thee with the *triṣṭubh* metre.
I cover you with the Jāgata metre;
may Vāc cover you;
may Urj cover you.
May the oblation satisfy you; satisfy your speech; satisfy your strength.
Cut the offering!
O God, you who move before us, may we accomplish you. 10.
Bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ, svaḥ, and vaṣaṭ—thus [he should recite]. || 3 ||

[4-4-1] O Brahman, we shall proceed with the Pravargya rite. O Hotṛ, recite the hymn for the Gharma. O Agnīdh, place the two Rauhina cakes upon the fire. O Pratiprasthātṛ, perform the distribution of the fires. O Prastotṛ, chant the Sāmans.

You who are yoked by the Yajus, anointed by the Sāmans, approved by all the gods and the Maruts, extended by the sacrificial gifts, and capable of carrying us across—may the chanters carry you forward as you are well-disposed. Bestow radiance upon us, being free from anger. Bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ.
"O you who possess Indra, proceed! (11). And two [verses] without resentment. (4)
[4-5-1] "O Brahman, we shall proceed with the ritual. O Hotṛ, recite the praise for the Gharma!
For Yama you, for Makha you!"
For the impetus of the Sun, thee!
Svāhā to the out-breath, svāhā to the diffused breath, svāhā to the in-breath! Svāhā to the eye, svāhā to the ear!
Hail to the mind! Hail to Vāc Sarasvatī! Hail to skill! Hail to resolve! Hail to vigor! Hail to strength!
May the divine Savitṛ anoint you with honey. 12.
Protect the earth from heat!
You are the flame, you are the radiance, you are the light, you are the heat. Sit down; you are great.
Grieve, O Agni, most beloved by the gods; O worthy of sacrifice, send forth your smokeless, ruddy, and beautiful flame, O praised one!

Him whom the inspired singers anoint as if spreading him out, heating him with fire like a fatty oblation—like a son in his father’s lap, the most beloved *gharma* has sat down upon Agni, bringing immortality. 13.
Invincible from the front; under the sovereignty of Agni:
grant me long life.
The one with sons is on the south; under the sovereignty of Indra, grant me progeny. The one providing a good seat is on the west.
Under the sovereign authority of the god Savitṛ, grant me vital breath. Āśruti is in the north. 14.
Under the overlordship of Mitra and Varuṇa: grant me hearing.
The separator is above. Under the overlordship of Bṛhaspati.
Grant me spiritual power; grant me sovereign power. Bestow radiance upon me; bestow luster upon me. Bestow glory upon me; bestow austerity upon me.
Bestow the mind upon me.
O Manu’s mare, you who have many sons;
protect me from all destructive powers. 15.
[4-5-5] May you be easy for me to approach; do not harm me. O Agni, burn up the enemies within;
burn up the curse of the hostile stranger. O Vasu, being observant, burn up those who are thoughtless.
May they stand around you, undecaying and tireless. You are the piled-up, you are the completely piled-up. *Svāhā*! Be enclosed by the Maruts. You are *mā*.
You are the measure; you are the counterpart. 16.
[4-5-6] You are a measure; you are a counter-measure.
You are the one who drives away [evil].
You are the inner space of the intermediate region.
Protect the sky from heat. By these songs, whatever of ours is deficient here—
Swell up, O Lord of the bay horses, as you grow strong;

when you shatter the great enclosures for the sake of your praisers, may we then be the ones who receive the greatest portion of your bounty. One of your forms is radiant, the other is worthy of sacrifice. 17.
[4-5-7] You are like the sky with its two days of different forms; for you,
O self-dependent one, protect all wondrous powers.
O Pūṣan, may your bounty be auspicious here for us;
you deserve to carry your arrows and your bow;
you deserve the golden neck-ornament, worthy of sacrifice, which possesses every form.
O Worthy One, you take pity on this entire world;
there is nothing more powerful than you, O Rudra.
You are the Gāyatra.
Thou art of the Tristubh metre; thou art of the Jagatī metre; honey, honey, honey. 18.
Anaktva, sit down; protect us from the north. You are a counterpart; yours is another [portion] dedicated to the sacrifice, which is Jāgata, and there is one more. 5.

In life-span, in vital energy, in splendor, and in glory. || 86 ||
With glory and with the splendor of sacred knowledge.
